subject: general
question: Which of the following countries withdrew from the OCED Global Tax Deal in January 2025?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**USA**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **USA** withdrew from the **OECD Global Tax Deal** in January 2025, citing concerns over its implications for the country’s tax policies and sovereignty.
 
• The **OECD Global Tax Deal** was designed to establish a global framework for **minimum corporate tax rates** and ensure multinational corporations pay taxes where they generate revenue.
 
• The USA’s withdrawal can be attributed to **domestic political opposition**, as certain political factions argued the deal could disadvantage US-based businesses or reduce the government’s control over tax rules.
 
• This decision impacted global efforts to create a more equitable taxation system and raised concerns regarding the future of multilateral agreements in the realm of international taxation.
 
• The USA has significant influence over global economic policies, and its withdrawal from the OECD deal created challenges for other nations in implementing the agreed framework effectively.
 
• The OECD tax deal was particularly aimed at addressing issues like **tax avoidance** by multinational corporations and establishing a fair tax regime for the digital economy.
 
• Countries that remained committed to the OECD Global Tax Deal had to re-evaluate their strategies and mechanisms to ensure the deal’s success despite the USA’s absence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Russia**__

 __
 
• **Russia** is one of the largest economies but has not been a significant proponent of global tax reforms like the OECD deal.
 
• Its tax system is structured differently, focusing on domestic priorities rather than international frameworks.
 
• Russia has often maintained a cautious stance in joining global economic agreements, citing concerns over sovereignty.
 
 
 
• **India**__
 __
 
• **India** has actively supported the OECD Global Tax Deal and played a key role in international discussions on digital taxation.
 
• India has advocated for fair taxation of multinational corporations operating in developing economies.
 
• The country has implemented its own measures, such as the **Equalisation Levy**, targeting digital services provided by foreign entities.
 
 
 
• **China**__
 
 
• **China** has shown support for global tax reforms under the OECD framework but has emphasized aligning these with its own economic priorities.
 
• China’s participation in such deals is often strategic, aiming to maintain its economic competitiveness globally.
